title: feat: opt-in HW acceleration for 2020 5K iMacs (Navi 14)
head: a99ecf31c605
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A failure after the accelerated build can leave the supposedly safe UKI accelerated
leads.consequence: The first limine-mkinitcpio replaces omarchy_linux-t2.efi with an image lacking nomodeset. If the second rebuild fails or power is lost before it finishes, the EXIT trap restores only the drop-in; --rebuild removes the extra entry, but the original/default UKI can still boot with the unsafe flags. The next pacman hook invocation sees no hwaccel copy and exits without repairing that UKI. The success test's FAIL_MKINITCPIO stub fails the first build, never this path.

leads.summary: The installed upgrade hook misses all non-linux-t2 UKI regenerations
leads.consequence: Updating firmware or mkinitcpio, changing hibernation/resume parameters, or calling omarchy-plymouth-set/limine-mkinitcpio rebuilds the default UKI while leaving the accelerated copy stale. It can retain outdated initramfs, root/unlock/resume options, or modules after a non-linux-t2 update. The next linux-t2 upgrade is the only automatic repair; for example hibernation setup immediately writes resume= and rebuilds the safe image but not the accelerated one.

leads.summary: Signed Snapper UKIs contain no .cmdline section, so opt-in cannot work on that supported configuration
leads.consequence: On systems with sbctl keys installed and Snapper configured, upstream limine-mkinitcpio deliberately builds UKIs with --no-cmdline, using the cmdline in limine.conf instead. objcopy --only-section=.cmdline cannot find accelerated flags, so the command exits before creating its entry. Merely skipping the check would not help: --add-efi emits a top-level EFI chainload with no cmdline, rather than a linux-t2 kernel entry with an associated cmdline.

leads.summary: Removing an accelerated default loses the previous default and can select the wrong OS
leads.consequence: --default replaces the existing default_entry (Omarchy's template sets 2); --remove and a failed --rebuild then comment it out rather than restore its former value. Limine falls back to entry 1, which can be a different OS or EFI loader instead of the promised safe Omarchy entry. The test starts with a commented placeholder, so it cannot detect this regression. remember_last_entry, when enabled, also supersedes --default.

leads.summary: Changing default_entry with sed bypasses Limine's configured config enrollment
leads.consequence: On installs that enable ENABLE_ENROLL_LIMINE_CONFIG=yes, upstream --add-efi/--remove-efi-path run post hooks which enroll/sign limine.conf; the subsequent --default or --remove sed modifies it without re-enrolling. Limine detects a different checksum and refuses the boot. The same applies when --rebuild drops the default after a failure. Enrollment is optional, so this is conditional, not a failure on the shipped default.

leads.summary: The copy and config location do not follow an alternate ESP_PATH (overlapping open PR #7410)
leads.consequence: The dependency follows ESP_PATH when building its UKI and editing the real limine.conf, but this command always reads /boot/EFI/Linux/omarchy_linux-t2.efi and edits /boot/limine.conf. For T2 overlay installations on /boot/efi, as explicitly supported by open PR #7410, the copy/check fails because the built UKI is in /boot/efi/EFI/Linux, and --default/--remove would edit the wrong configuration. The PRs touch different paths, so no textual merge resolves this.
leads.triage: verified factual (#7410 open, /boot/efi ESP); not published: depends on unmerged PR

leads.summary: Rebuilding overwrites administrator additions in the iMac display drop-in
leads.consequence: The opt-in command rewrites the whole existing imac20-display.conf twice, restoring only two fixed safe flags, not its original bytes. Any user-added kernel parameters or comments in that file are lost even on a successful opt-in; an EXIT trap after a failure does the same. Changing an existing drop-in should preserve unrelated configuration.
leads.triage: not published: Omarchy-owned drop-in rewritten whole elsewhere too

leads.summary: The detector also gates --remove, preventing cleanup after detection stops working
leads.consequence: If DMI/product_name or the PCI device files are missing or the GPU no longer enumerates, --remove prints 'nothing to do' and returns success, leaving the active boot entry and pacman hook in place. A recovery/disable operation need not depend on the hardware still being detectable; the hook then likewise cannot clean it on a failed kernel rebuild.
leads.triage: verified (detector gates --remove); not published: low impact

leads.summary: Related open documentation PR #10783 duplicates the 2020 iMac line
leads.consequence: The independently open #10783 adds a second A2115 (iMac20,1/iMac20,2) bullet, and its diff applies cleanly onto this head at line 69. If both merge without reconciliation the same machine appears twice under T2 devices. #10783 is diverged, not stacked; GitHub currently reports MERGEABLE relative to its own base.

leads.summary: The new opt-in test stubs away the two failure boundaries it claims to check
leads.consequence: Its limine-mkinitcpio stub produces a text file containing only display flags rather than a bootable UKI with root/LUKS parameters and cannot fail only the second build; its limine-entry-tool stub never changes limine.conf except removing the copied image. The remove assertion checks the image and hook, not that --remove removed a Limine menu entry. A plausible broken live implementation that leaves the Limine entry registered still passes these assertions, and H1/H4 remain invisible. Add a second-build failure case and assert the actual menu entry and prior default with an authentic Limine config/fixture.

leads.summary: The claimed stock linux-t2 patch may not cover every Navi 14 configuration admitted by the detector
leads.consequence: The available upstream T2 6001 patch bypasses SMU allowed-mask setup only for vendor/device 1002:7340 AND subsystem 106b:0219, while the detector accepts all display-class 1002:7340 GPUs on iMac20,1/2 and the manual names both 5300 and 5500. If a listed GPU has a different subsystem ID, the patch's workaround does not run, so acceleration remains a hardware experiment. This is not evidence of an actual 5500 failure: settle it from linux-t2's installed package revision and the PCI subsystem IDs of both affected iMac models (or a boot test).

limits: No iMac/Navi 14 hardware or bootloader execution: all hardware/driver behavior beyond the pinned scripts and upstream source is untested. Upstream limine-entry-tool was fetched from AUR's 1.40.0 recipe; Omarchy does not pin the installed package version. Live filesystem overlays, Secure Boot firmware and a signed kernel were not booted. Other open PRs discovered by broad keyword searches beyond the overlapping candidates in inventory.json were not merged or executed.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12524#issuecomment-5828129207) and the [author's update](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12524#issuecomment-5843935468), checked at `a99ecf3`.

**Verified:** all four earlier findings and both notes are resolved at this head.

| Earlier claim | Status at `a99ecf3` |
|---|---|
| Fresh installs halt during hardware setup | Resolved. `install-imac20-amdgpu-hwaccel.sh` is deleted, and `fix-imac20-display.sh` is the only iMac20 step left in `all.sh`. The test asserts that the HW-accel command stays out of `all.sh`. |
| No `imac20-hwaccel` boot entry | Resolved. `limine-entry-tool --add-efi` registers the copied UKI as its own top-level entry. It has no `cmdline:` line, so the UKI's embedded command line is used. That command line is linux-t2's full one, with `amdgpu.modeset=1 video=efifb:off` in place of `nomodeset`. `--default` sets a `default_entry` path that Limine accepts. |
| Companion build is machine-specific and unpinned | Resolved. No clone, module build or companion reference remains. |
| linux-t2 already applies 6001 | Resolved. The rebuild, the constant scan and the inverted backup check are gone. What made `amdgpu` bind is still open, as the author notes (see the last section). |
| Command note (no elevation, `OMARCHY_PATH` under `sudo`) | Resolved. Root writes go through `sudo` inside the command, and nothing sources `$OMARCHY_PATH`. |
| Test note (failing test, host paths) | Resolved. `imac20-amdgpu-hwaccel-test.sh` passes 6/6, and every path goes through the `OMARCHY_*` overrides into a temp directory. Nine mutants of the command (for example no trap, no `set_default`, no hook) all fail the test. |

The first commit (the #12203 fallback) is unchanged, and `imac20-display-test.sh` still passes 11/11, including on a local merge with the `quattro` tip at `bf44355`.

The reworked command has two new problems, both on its failure and removal paths, plus two smaller notes.

### A failed or interrupted second build leaves the default entries on the HW-accel command line

`build_entry` uses the default UKI as scratch space. `limine-mkinitcpio` with no arguments rebuilds every installed kernel's UKI and rewrites each entry's `cmdline:` in `limine.conf`. So between the first build and the second, the normal "Omarchy" entries boot without `nomodeset`:

```text
write drop-in: HW-accel flags        trap set: restore drop-in only
limine-mkinitcpio                    default UKIs now HW-accel     <- window opens
cp default UKI -> hwaccel UKI
write drop-in: safe flags            trap cleared (line 59)
limine-mkinitcpio                    default UKIs safe again       <- window closes
limine-entry-tool --add-efi
```

The EXIT trap only rewrites the drop-in and never rebuilds, and it is cleared before the second full rebuild. Sandboxed runs of the command with stubbed `limine-mkinitcpio`, `limine-entry-tool` and `objcopy` gave:

| Case | Exit | Drop-in | Default linux-t2 UKI and its `cmdline:` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Second build fails | 1 | safe | HW-accel |
| `cp` fails | 1 | safe | HW-accel |
| Ctrl-C, SIGHUP or SIGTERM after the first build | 130 / 129 / 143 | safe | HW-accel |
| Hook `--rebuild`, second build fails (after `--default`) | 0 | safe | HW-accel; the `imac20-hwaccel` entry is removed |
| Hook `--rebuild`, `cp` fails | 0 | safe | safe; the previous kernel's HW-accel UKI stays registered, with no message |

The last row is silent because `(build_entry)` runs as an `if !` condition (line 106), where bash ignores `set -e`. Only the two explicit command-line checks and the final `limine-entry-tool` status can fail it. The real `limine-mkinitcpio` also exits 0 when a per-kernel build fails, so failures reach the command-line check rather than stopping at the build call. Where the first build produces no `.cmdline` (UKIs disabled, or `sbctl` together with Snapper, where limine-mkinitcpio-hook builds without one), the first check always fails after the HW-accel flags are already in every entry. Neither is the default on a UEFI Omarchy install.

**Impact:** on the machines this PR targets, an interrupted opt-in or a failing rebuild during a `linux-t2` upgrade can leave the default entries on the unverified HW-accel path, which the safe entry exists to avoid. The hook does remove the HW-accel entry as described, but the next boot does not fall back to safe, because the default entries keep the HW-accel command line.

**Suggested change:** build the second UKI directly instead of through the default one, as limine-mkinitcpio-install does internally:

1. Take the last line of `limine-entry-tool --get-cmdline linux-t2` (as root; upstream uses `| tail -n 1`).
2. Swap `nomodeset` for the HW-accel flags and write the result to a temp file.
3. Build with `/usr/bin/mkinitcpio --kernel <version> --cmdline <file> --uki <temp>`. Use the explicit `/usr/bin` path: the hook package's `/usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio` wrapper returns 0 for non-preset calls whatever mkinitcpio did.
4. Verify the result, move it into place and run `--add-efi`.

This never touches the default entries and drops the drop-in swap and the second full rebuild. If the current design stays, the trap needs to restore and rebuild, and `--rebuild` needs an explicit check after each step.

### `--remove` drops Omarchy's `default_entry` instead of restoring it

Omarchy's `/boot/limine.conf` comes from `default/limine/limine.conf`, which has `default_entry: 2`. `--default` rewrites that line to `default_entry: imac20-hwaccel`. `remove_entry` (line 46) then rewrites it to `#default_entry: <OS name>/<kernel name>`, so no default is set.

```text
installed         default_entry: 2               -> Omarchy/linux-t2, autoboots
--default         default_entry: imac20-hwaccel
--remove          #default_entry: <OS name>/...  -> unset -> entry 1 = "Omarchy" directory
```

With `default_entry` unset (and no `LoaderEntryDefault` EFI variable or `remember_last_entry`, which Omarchy does not set), Limine 12.9 selects entry 1. In Omarchy's layout that is the `/+Omarchy` directory, and a selected directory disables autoboot. This is from Limine's `menu.c`, a model of that selection applied to the `limine.conf` from an omarchy-iso fresh install, and a sandboxed run of the command. The run shows `default_entry: 2` replaced after `--default` then `--remove`, and kept when `--remove` runs without `--default`. A failed hook rebuild while the HW-accel entry is the default takes the same path. The test misses this because its fixture starts from limine-entry-tool's own template line (`#default_entry: <OS name>/<kernel name>`), not Omarchy's `default_entry: 2`.

**Impact:** after the documented `--default` then `--remove` flow, every boot stops at the Limine menu until `limine.conf` is edited or `omarchy-refresh-limine` runs. Meanwhile the command reports "only the safe entry remains".

**Suggested change:** save the replaced `default_entry` line when `--default` runs and restore it on removal, or write `default_entry: 2` back. In the test, seed Omarchy's template and assert that `default_entry: 2` is kept without `--default` and comes back after `--remove` and after a failed rebuild. Seeding alone is not enough: the current assertions still pass on the current behaviour once the `#default_entry:` check is adjusted.

### Smaller notes on the hook and `--default`

**Stale HW-accel UKI:** the hook triggers only on the `linux-t2` package. The default UKIs are also rebuilt by `90-mkinitcpio-install.hook` (firmware, systemd, cryptsetup and similar paths) and by `omarchy-hibernation-setup`/`-remove` and `omarchy-plymouth-set`, none of which refresh the HW-accel copy. With `--default`, the machine then boots an older initramfs and command line (for example without a new `resume=`) until the next `linux-t2` upgrade or a manual re-run. Suggested change: give the hook the same triggers as `90-mkinitcpio-install.hook`, or document that the command should be re-run after those changes. The code comment "limine-mkinitcpio only builds the default UKI" is also inaccurate: without arguments it rebuilds every installed kernel.

**Enrolled config:** `--default` and `--remove` edit `limine.conf` with `sed` after limine-entry-tool's post hooks have run. With `ENABLE_ENROLL_LIMINE_CONFIG=yes` in `/etc/default/limine` (not an Omarchy default), the enrolled checksum no longer matches and Limine refuses the config. Running `limine-enroll-config` after the edit, as limine-entry-tool's own hook does, avoids it.

### Open question: which change made `amdgpu` bind

The update says the source of the fix is not isolated. A source reading of Linux 7.2 suggests the two new flags may be inert on this kernel, which would point to the `linux-t2` update:

- `amdgpu.modeset` is only consulted when `nomodeset` is set. Without `nomodeset`, `=1` behaves like the default.
- `video=efifb:off` is read only by `efifb`. linux-t2 7.2.6.arch2-4 has `CONFIG_SYSFB_SIMPLEFB=y` and `CONFIG_DRM_SIMPLEDRM=y`, so for a simplefb-compatible GOP mode the firmware framebuffer is claimed by `simpledrm` and `efifb` never probes.

This is a hypothesis, not tested on hardware, and whether the iMac's GOP mode is simplefb-compatible was not checked. On an HW-accel boot, `journalctl -k -b | grep -Ei 'simple-framebuffer|simpledrm|efifb'` would show which framebuffer driver ran. One boot with only `nomodeset` removed would show whether the extra flags matter. If they do not, dropping `nomodeset` for known-good kernels could replace the second UKI.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of `a99ecf3` against the earlier head, limine-entry-tool/limine-mkinitcpio-hook 1.39.0 (the version packaged at PR time; the relevant behaviour is the same in 1.40.0), Limine 12.9.0, omarchy-iso's install flow, pacman hook ordering and Linux 7.2 framebuffer/amdgpu code. Sandboxed runs: both PR tests at the head and on a local merge with `quattro`, mutants of the HW-accel test, the command with stubbed `limine-mkinitcpio`, `limine-entry-tool` and `objcopy` under success, failure and signal cases, real `objcopy` on synthetic PE files with a `.cmdline` section, and a model of Limine's default-entry selection. No iMac hardware, real boot, real `limine-mkinitcpio` run or Secure Boot setup. The author's hardware results were not reproduced.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
